title: Admit distinct queries, suppress duplicate in-flight work
contract: Implement shouldFetch(active, next). active is null or {status, query}; next is {search,status,page,limit}. Return false only if an identical query is already loading. Compare the four query values, not object identity or JSON property order. Return true for changed queries, completed/failed requests, or no active request. Do not suppress all requests merely because one is loading.
hints: A loading request for one search must not block a different search.
Compare stable primitive query fields; two object instances can describe the same request.

tests.name: Suppress a duplicate described by a fresh object
tests.explanation: Equivalent values identify duplicate work even when property order differs.

tests.name: Allow a newer search while the old query is loading
tests.explanation: A blanket loading guard would lose the latest user query.

tests.name: Pagination changes are distinct queries
tests.explanation: Page is part of the request identity.

tests.name: Allow retrying the same failed request
tests.explanation: A failed request is no longer in flight.

tests.name: Allow the first request
tests.explanation: No active work means nothing to deduplicate.

tests.name: Status and page size also distinguish requests
tests.explanation: Every documented query field participates in identity.

businessContext: Every time a parent component re-renders or the user tabs between drawer views, duplicate identical GET requests hit the `/api/applications` and `/api/dashboard/stats` endpoints.
productionSymptom: Backend servers experience 4x expected QPS. Database connection pools spike under moderate user load.
